drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel:
Thank you for your note. We have taken a pass at the draft to bridge toward a more customary acquisition agreement while keeping the document appropriately streamlined for this transaction.

Seller is prepared to move materially on price and structure, but not to an open-ended diligence option or a full buyer-form risk allocation. The attached reflects a counterproposal at USD 42,000,000, with limited cash/debt mechanics and a targeted package of representations, conditions, covenants, indemnity, confidentiality and termination provisions. We have included Buyer protections where appropriate, but have kept them tied to objective standards, materiality, and reasonable caps/limitations.

If helpful, we can use this as the working draft rather than exchanging a full buyer-side form at this stage.

edits.text: 1. Purchase Price. The Buyer shall pay the Seller USD 42,000,000 for the Shares (the "Purchase Price"). The Purchase Price is based on the Company being delivered at Closing on a cash-free, debt-free basis, with any unpaid funded indebtedness and transaction expenses of the Company or Seller to be discharged at or prior to Closing or deducted from the Purchase Price. The Purchase Price shall not be subject to any post-Closing working-capital adjustment unless the parties agree in writing on a target working-capital amount, included and excluded line items, and a final adjustment mechanism prior to signing.

2. Closing. Closing shall occur on the fifth Business Day after satisfaction or waiver of the conditions expressly set forth in this Agreement, or on such other date as the parties may agree in writing; provided that the Closing shall occur no later than 30 days after signing unless extended by mutual written agreement. At Closing, Seller shall deliver instruments of transfer for the Shares, and Buyer shall pay the Purchase Price by wire transfer of immediately available funds.

3. Representations. Seller represents and warrants to Buyer that: (a) Seller has full power and authority to enter into and perform this Agreement and to sell the Shares; (b) Seller owns the Shares free and clear of liens other than restrictions arising under applicable securities laws or this Agreement; (c) the execution, delivery and performance of this Agreement by Seller have been duly authorized and do not violate any organizational document or material contract binding on Seller; (d) the financial statements delivered to Buyer fairly present, in all material respects, the financial position and results of operations of the Company as of the dates and for the periods indicated, subject in the case of unaudited statements to normal year-end adjustments and the absence of footnotes; (e) to Seller's knowledge, since the date of the most recent financial statements, there has not occurred any material adverse change in the business, assets, financial condition or results of operations of the Company, taken as a whole; (f) to Seller's knowledge, the Company is in material compliance with applicable laws, has filed material tax returns required to be filed and paid material taxes due, and is not subject to any pending material litigation; (g) to Seller's knowledge, the material contracts, intellectual property, employee benefit arrangements and permits of the Company made available to Buyer are sufficient in all material respects for the conduct of the business as currently conducted; and (h) no broker or finder has been engaged by Seller for whom Buyer or the Company will be liable. Except for the representations and warranties expressly set forth in this Agreement, Seller makes no other representation or warranty, express or implied, including with respect to projections, forecasts or other forward-looking information.

4. Confidentiality. Each party shall keep confidential the terms of this Agreement and non-public information received from the other party or concerning the Company in connection with the transactions contemplated hereby, except that disclosure may be made to such party's affiliates and its and their respective representatives, financing sources, insurers, tax advisers and legal advisers who are informed of the confidential nature of the information, and as required by applicable law, regulation, stock exchange rule, court order or governmental authority. This Section does not restrict disclosure of information that is or becomes publicly available other than through breach of this Agreement, was already known to the receiving party without restriction, or is independently developed without use of confidential information.

5. Conditions to Closing. Buyer's obligation to close is subject only to the following conditions: (a) Seller's fundamental representations regarding authority and title to the Shares shall be true and correct in all material respects at signing and Closing; (b) Seller's other representations shall be true and correct at signing and Closing except where the failure to be true and correct has not had and would not reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect on the Company, taken as a whole; (c) Seller shall have performed in all material respects its covenants required to be performed prior to Closing; (d) any governmental approvals legally required for consummation of the sale of the Shares shall have been obtained; and (e) no court or governmental authority shall have issued an order prohibiting Closing. Completion of Buyer's diligence shall not be a condition to Closing, it being understood that Buyer will complete its confirmatory diligence before signing.

6. Interim Covenants. From signing until Closing, except as required by law, expressly contemplated by this Agreement, disclosed to Buyer prior to signing, or approved by Buyer in writing (such approval not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed), Seller shall cause the Company to operate in the ordinary course of business in all material respects and shall not cause the Company to: (a) issue equity securities; (b) incur material funded indebtedness outside the ordinary course; (c) sell or dispose of material assets outside the ordinary course; (d) enter into, materially amend or terminate any material contract outside the ordinary course; (e) declare or pay dividends or distributions other than cash distributions made prior to Closing and reflected in the cash-free/debt-free mechanics; (f) enter into material related-party transactions; or (g) materially increase compensation or benefits except in the ordinary course, as required by existing arrangements, or as required by law.

7. Indemnification. From and after Closing, Seller shall indemnify Buyer for direct out-of-pocket losses actually incurred by Buyer arising from any breach of Seller's representations, warranties or covenants in this Agreement, pre-Closing taxes of the Company, and pre-Closing liabilities of the Company to the extent not reflected in the Purchase Price mechanics or in the financial statements delivered to Buyer. Non-fundamental representations shall survive for 12 months after Closing and shall be subject to a deductible basket equal to 1.0% of the Purchase Price and an aggregate cap equal to 10% of the Purchase Price. Fundamental representations regarding authority and title to the Shares shall survive for six years and shall be capped at the Purchase Price. Seller shall not be liable for consequential, punitive, special or multiple-based damages except to the extent awarded to a third party. Nothing in this Section limits liability for actual fraud.

8. Termination. This Agreement may be terminated prior to Closing: (a) by mutual written agreement of Buyer and Seller; (b) by either party if Closing has not occurred by the outside date specified in Section 2, provided that the terminating party is not then in material breach of this Agreement; (c) by either party if a final, non-appealable order prohibits the Closing; or (d) by the non-breaching party if the other party has materially breached this Agreement and such breach has not been cured within 10 Business Days after written notice, to the extent curable. Upon termination, this Agreement shall be of no further force except for confidentiality, governing law, expenses and other provisions that by their nature should survive.

receiver.message_back:
Thank you for the revised draft. Buyer appreciates Seller’s movement and agrees this can serve as the working draft, subject to several points that are important to Buyer given the limited diligence completed to date and the seller-favorable risk allocation in the current draft.

Buyer’s counter is as follows:

1. Purchase Price. Buyer can proceed at USD 39,000,000, subject to the protections below. The current USD 42,000,000 proposal does not yet reflect the remaining diligence uncertainty or the limited representation/indemnity package.

2. Price Mechanics. The agreement should include customary cash-free/debt-free mechanics and a normalized working-capital adjustment. We propose a target based on the trailing 12-month average working capital, with agreed included/excluded line items. Indebtedness, Seller/Company transaction expenses, change-of-control payments and unpaid pre-Closing taxes should reduce the price dollar-for-dollar.

3. Missing Sections. The draft jumps from Section 3 to Section 8. Your cover note refers to confidentiality, covenants, indemnity and conditions, but those provisions are not included in the visible draft we received. Please circulate the complete draft or insert those provisions.

4. Representations. The current representations remain too limited and too heavily knowledge/materiality-qualified. Buyer needs customary private-company acquisition reps, including capitalization, title to assets, absence of undisclosed liabilities, material contracts, IP, employees/benefits, taxes, compliance, permits, litigation, environmental, related-party matters and brokers. Knowledge qualifiers should be limited to areas where appropriate.

5. Covenants / Access. Please add interim operating covenants requiring the Company to operate in the ordinary course and restricting material actions without Buyer consent, plus reasonable access to information, management and records through Closing.

6. Conditions. Closing should be conditioned on accuracy of representations, covenant compliance, receipt of required approvals/consents, no material adverse effect, delivery of closing documents and satisfactory completion of confirmatory diligence.

7. Indemnity. Buyer requires an indemnity package: 18-month survival for general reps, longer survival for fundamental and tax reps, a 0.75% basket, 10% cap for general reps, purchase-price cap or uncapped recovery for fundamental reps and fraud, and no limitations for fraud or intentional misconduct.

8. Timing / Termination. The 30-day outside date is too short if approvals, diligence or financing logistics remain open. Please revise to 60 days after signing, with extension for pending required approvals, provided the parties are working in good faith.

9. No-Reliance / Confidentiality. The no-reliance language should not limit express representations, fraud claims or disclosures in schedules. Confidentiality should be mutual and include customary exceptions for required disclosures and disclosures to advisers, financing sources and representatives.

If Seller can meet Buyer at USD 39,000,000 with these core protections, Buyer is prepared to move promptly on a markup and closing process.
